text:
maya: seeing a spike in failed SSO auths and account lockouts since 03:14 UTC, looks like impossible-travel across regions for the same user IDs :rotating_light:

ops-bot: ALERT: auth.pipeline.high-fail-rate 2255012345 - 3.2k failures in last 10m, peak 03:16 UTC

sam: ack. quick question — how many unique accounts affected and which apps?

maya: ~210 unique users, concentrated on 'console-prod' and 'api-key-manager'. sample IPs: 45.120.12.9, 2.56.89.120, 185.63.24.10. Many MFA pushes showing "denied" on the IDP side, but also a flood of auth attempts with spoofed user-agents. MFA fatigue suspected.

lee: can we temp throttle /sso/authorize and raise lockout threshold? also recommend adding those CIDRs to blocklist for now.

andrew: before we block, check IDP logs for normal SSO flow changes (might be a vendor side surge). also pull KMS audit for any unusual key operations tied to session revokes — just in case refresh tokens were used.

natalie: CS reporting ~15 escalations asking "why am I getting push requests?" — want a short blurb we can send to affected customers.

maya: ran quick EL query (auth-logs index):
```
index=auth-logs | where timestamp>ago(15m) and event=\"sso_failure\" | summarize count() by src_ip, user_agent, user_id | sort by count desc
```
results show repeated patterns from ~30 IPs, and a handful of CI/service accounts with high velocity.

sam: containment steps I'm taking now:
- add blocklist CIDRs: 45.120.0.0/16, 185.63.0.0/16
- set rate-limit on /sso/authorize to 10 reqs/min per IP
- force token revocation for affected user_ids (script: `scripts/auth/revoke_sessions --user-list suspicious.txt`)
Link: https://internal/redwood/ops/auth-actions

ir-bot: action: sessions revoked for 198 accounts by sam at 03:22 UTC

lee: noticed false positives: three service accounts used for scheduled infra jobs got locked. adding them to temporary allowlist and will update RBAC to mark service accounts exempt from user lockout.

natalie: do we want to tell customers to reset passwords or just to reauthenticate?

maya: reauth only — no evidence of credentials exfil. instruct users to accept an auth and re-register push if they had it — we will not force password reset. draft blurb: \"We've detected unusual sign-in activity and temporarily revoked sessions. If you see unexpected pushes, deny them and re-authenticate via SSO. Contact support if you still can't sign in.\"

sam: follow-ups for post-incident:
- tune detection: add user-agent anomaly score, strict impossible-travel window, and MFA-push-frequency detector
- add CI/service-account allowlist auto-detection to avoid collateral lockouts
- create runbook step: run `k8s-auth-proxy rotate --session-revokes` and capture KMS audit entries

maya: assigning owners: detection tuning -> sam (48h), runbook updates -> lee (72h), CS blurb + follow-up comms -> natalie (ASAP), collect KMS + IDP logs -> andrew (24h).

andrew: I'll pull KMS HSM audit and IDP assertion logs and drop to the incident ticket. if we see any HKDF/signature anomalies we'll escalate.

maya: agreed. interim verdict: MFA fatigue + scripted credential stuffing + user-agent spoofing. containment successful for now, monitoring for 2h. creating incident ticket INC-2025-142 and scheduling postmortem.

natalie: putting the CS blurb into zendesk and sending to affected org contacts.

sam: landing item: add a new alert for \"mfa-push-density\" and a playbook step to check RBAC allowlist before mass revokes.

maya: thanks all. will update thread with timeline + evidence once andrew drops KMS/IDP logs.
